title: Fetch, Render and Store
summary: Loading JSON into the page, loading and error states, and localStorage.

steps.title: Fetch and render
body: The classic browser loop: fetch JSON, turn it into HTML, put it on the page, and handle the in-between states.
app.innerHTML = renderTodos(todos);         // renderTodos escapes the titles

Every data view has at least three states: **loading**, **error**, and **loaded** (and often a fourth, **empty**). Forgetting one is the most common UI bug. React apps model them as a discriminated union, and a single `render(state)` function decides what to show.

> **Try it:** open the **Playground**, choose the **HTML/CSS/JS** tab and paste the HTML and script from this card. The live preview runs it in a real browser frame, and the **Tailwind** switch lets you style it with utility classes.

steps.title: localStorage
body: `localStorage` keeps **strings** in the browser per site, surviving reloads (about 5 MB):

Treat what you read back as untrusted: it can be missing, from an older version of your app, or edited by hand in dev tools. Parse it in a `try`, validate it, and fall back to a default. Never store secrets or tokens there: any script on the page can read it.
`sessionStorage` has the same API but is cleared when the tab closes. In Next.js, `localStorage` only exists in the **browser**, not during server rendering.

steps.explain: Storage converts everything to strings. Use JSON for anything that is not a string.

steps.prompt: Complete the code that saves and restores a cart.
A tiny render function picks the state to show. What does this print?
code: type View = { status: "loading" } | { status: "error"; message: string } | { status: "loaded"; items: string[] };
console.log([show({ status: "loading" }), show({ status: "loaded", items: [] }), show({ status: "loaded", items: ["a", "b"] }), show({ status: "error", message: "500" })].join(" "));
steps.explain: One function maps every state to output, so no state can be forgotten. This is exactly what a React component does.

steps.title: A safe storage wrapper
prompt: Write `loadPrefs(storage: StorageLike): Prefs` and `savePrefs(storage: StorageLike, prefs: Prefs): void` using the key `"prefs"`.
type StorageLike = { getItem(k: string): string | null; setItem(k: string, v: string): void };

`loadPrefs` returns the defaults `{ theme: "light", pageSize: 20 }` when the key is missing or the JSON is broken, and otherwise merges valid fields over the defaults: `theme` must be `"light"` or `"dark"`, `pageSize` an integer 5 to 100. Invalid fields keep their default.
The tests pass a fake in-memory storage (it has the same shape as `localStorage`).

if (typeof r.pageSize === "number" && Number.isInteger(r.pageSize) && r.pageSize >= 5 && r.pageSize <= 100) prefs.pageSize = r.pageSize;
